overview.description: Doppelkopf (meaning 'Double Head') is Germany's most widely played trick-taking card game, deeply embedded in German social culture. It is played with 48 cards (double deck of 9-A in 4 suits). Crucially, partnerships are NOT fixed â€” they are determined secretly each hand by who holds the two Queens of Clubs. Players use bidding signals to find their partner. The trump suit is extensive: all Queens, all Jacks, and all Diamonds are permanent trump.

history.origins: Doppelkopf evolved from Schafkopf in Northern Germany. Its name refers to playing with a 'double head' (double deck). It is referenced as early as the 19th century but became codified in the 20th century through the German Doppelkopf Association.
timeline: 1900s: Spreads across Germany. Regional rules diverge.
1995: German Doppelkopf Association publishes official tournament rules.
Present: Most popular card game in Germany by active players.
history.evolution: The key evolutionary feature is the dynamic, secret partnership determined by the Queens of Clubs. This transforms every hand into a social deduction problemâ€”players must figure out who their partner is while also playing out tricks correctly.
history.cultural: A national institution in Germany. Often played in dedicated Doppelkopf clubs ('Vereine'). Strongly regionalâ€”North German rules differ significantly from South German. Germany's Doppelkopf Association (DKV) governs official rules.

setup.players: Doppelkopf is played by exactly four players in the standard game. Two form the Re team and two form Kontra; the partnership is not fixed at the start—it is determined secretly by who holds the Queens of Clubs. With five people present, the game can be played with the dealer sitting out each hand.
setup.deck: 48 cards: Double deck of 9-10-J-Q-K-A in 4 suits (9s to Aces); 8s and below discarded. Each rank appears TWICE.
setup.equipment: Cards. Score sheet or Ramsch log.

rules.objective: The Re team (holders of Queens of Clubs) aims to score 121+ of 240 card points; Kontra aims to score 120+.
rules.gameplay: Must follow suit; if void of led suit, may play any card (including trump). Highest trump wins; else highest of led suit. Winner leads next trick.
keyRules: All Queens and all Jacks and all Diamonds are trumpâ€”a very large trump suit.
The partnership is NOT known at the startâ€”you discover it through play.
Total card points = 240 (2 complete sets). Re needs 121 to win; Kontra needs 120.

strategy.basic: Hold your Queens of Clubsâ€”they're the key to identifying your partner. Lead the â™£Q only when you want to reveal your partnership.
strategy.intermediate: Trump Management: With 12 trump cards total in play, careful trump counting is essential. If you hold 5+ trump, you can dominate the trump suit. Announce 'Re' early only if confidentâ€”it doubles the stakes.
strategy.advanced: Partnership Signaling Without Communication: Play the â™£Q underneath partner's trick to alert them. Discard high-point cards when partner has a certain trump winner to maximize points captured. Counter-Announcements: If Re announces, Kontra should announce back only with strong hands (3+ high trump).
tips: The tens of Hearts is the 'Dulle' (most powerful non-trump Ace equivalent in many variants).
Hochzeit (Marriage): If you hold BOTH Queens of Clubs, you may announce 'Marriage'â€”your partner becomes whoever wins your first trick.

considerations: Dynamic partnership inference is the core unique challenge.

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: Heart 10 highest; then all Queens (Clubs, Spades, Hearts, Diamonds); then all Jacks; then Diamonds A, 10, K, 9. Off-suit: A, 10, K, 9.
trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Highest trump wins the trick; if no trump was played, highest card of the led suit wins. When two identical cards are played, the first one played wins.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Player to left of dealer leads first trick; thereafter winner of previous trick leads.

edgeCases.text: When two identical cards are played to the same trick, the first card played wins.
Hochzeit (Marriage): holder of both Queens of Clubs may announce Marriage; partner is the first other player to win a trick, or if Marriage holder wins first three tricks they play alone.
Ramsch: if all pass (no Vorbehalt), each plays for himself; player with most card points loses.
Silent solo: player with both Queens of Clubs who says Gesund plays alone against the other three without revealing.
Re needs 121 card points to win; if Kontra announced but not Re, Re needs only 120.
Announcements (Re, Kontra, No 90, No 60, No 30, Schwarz) require minimum cards in hand and increase game value; unfulfilled announcement loses the game.

customActions.description: Dealer shuffles, cards are cut, then all 48 cards are dealt out three at a time starting to dealer's left, clockwise; 12 cards each.
Announce Re to declare your team (holders of Queens of Clubs) and commit to scoring at least 121 card points; increases game value.
customActions.constraints: Re team only; with 11 or more cards in hand in normal game.

customActions.description: Announce Kontra to declare the opposing team and commit to holding Re to 120 or fewer card points; increases game value.
customActions.constraints: Kontra team only; with 10 or more cards in hand after Re announced, or 11+ if Re not yet announced.

customActions.description: Announce Hochzeit (Marriage): you hold both Queens of Clubs; your partner is the first other player to win a trick. If you win the first three tricks you play alone.
customActions.constraints: Only when holding both Queens of Clubs and saying Vorbehalt during bidding.

engine.deckDescription: Two heavily stripped French decks combined, totaling 48 cards with four suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades) and six ranks per suit (9 through Ace), created by removing all 2s through 8s from two standard 52-card decks.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits appearing twice: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card design and distinct color coding for easy identification of suit and deck.
engine.rankDescription: Twelve ranks total per suit (two of each from 9 through Ace), where each rank determines card strength and trick-winning potential in various games requiring extended card availability.
